result.question:
I think we're over-sampling Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I'd like to free up crew time if the oil is genuinely stable.

First, list every open and pending-approval oil sampling or DGA work order on Transformer 1 over the next 90 days, with its number, scheduled date and assigned technician.

Then build two findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. TDCG at the first and last complete sample, using only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, with the IEEE C57.104 condition for each. Condition 1 is up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 is 721 to 1920, Condition 3 is 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 is above 4630. Also give me the TDCG rate in ppm/day.
2. A forecast of TDCG 7 days ahead from the last sample, with an 80% upper bound.

Treat the oil as stable only if both samples are Condition 1, the rate is under 10 ppm/day, and the forecast upper bound stays under 720 ppm.

If it's stable:
- Keep only the earliest sampling job in each 90-day block.
- Cancel the others, citing the kept work order number and the evidence in the reason.
- Never cancel a job that is priority 1 or that mentions acetylene or arcing.

If any of the three conditions fails, cancel nothing. Tell me which condition failed and whether the current schedule is dense enough for that condition level.

Finish with a table of each sampling job and whether it was kept or cancelled. If fewer than two complete samples exist, don't forecast, cancel nothing, and say the stability can't be shown.
result.answer:
I have everything needed; no further calls required. Nothing was cancelled.

## Open / pending-approval oil sampling or DGA work orders — Transformer 1, MAIN, next 90 days

| WO | Status | Description | Scheduled date | Assigned technician | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | APPR | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); long description adds a confirmatory oil sample for lab DGA at the visit | None set (schedstart/targstart null) | None assigned (no wplabor) | 1 |

That is the only open or approved-pending WO on Transformer 1 (the other two open WOs at MAIN are Pump 3 and Chiller 6). It has no child tasks, and the site calendar shows nothing scheduled through 2026‑12‑29. There are no standalone routine sampling jobs — so the schedule is not dense; if anything it is thin.

## Finding 1 — TDCG (H2 + CH4 + C2H6 + C2H4 + C2H2 + CO), IEEE C57.104

Four complete daily samples exist (2024‑01‑15 to 01‑18).

| Sample | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO | TDCG (ppm) | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First – 2024‑01‑15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 | **32,441** | **Condition 4** (>4630) |
| Last – 2024‑01‑18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 | **32,340** | **Condition 4** (>4630) |

TDCG rate: (32,340 − 32,441) / 3 days = **−33.7 ppm/day** (flat to slightly falling; intermediate samples were 32,086 and 32,343, i.e. noise of ±200 ppm around ~32,300).

## Finding 2 — 7‑day TDCG forecast (to 2024‑01‑25)

Method note: no file‑materialization tool was available to feed the TSFM runner, so this is a least‑squares linear trend on the four samples with a prediction interval (2 residual df), stated transparently.

- Trend slope: −4.6 ppm/day; point forecast at +7 days: **≈32,260 ppm**
- 80% upper bound (90th percentile of the prediction interval): **≈33,650 ppm**
- Consistent with the prior forecast already logged on WO 1000051 (upper bound 32,969 ppm).

## Stability verdict — NOT stable; nothing cancelled

| Criterion | Threshold | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both samples Condition 1 | ≤720 ppm | Both ~32,400 ppm → Condition 4 | **FAIL** |
| Rate < 10 ppm/day | <10 | −33.7 ppm/day (falling) | Pass |
| Forecast 80% upper bound < 720 ppm | <720 | ≈33,650 ppm | **FAIL** |

**Which condition failed:** Condition (1) — both samples are IEEE Condition 4, roughly 45× the Condition‑1 ceiling and 7× the Condition‑4 threshold; consequently condition (3) also fails since the forecast cannot come anywhere near 720 ppm. Only the rate criterion passes, and a flat rate at Condition 4 means "stably very bad", not "healthy". The gas signature (ethylene ≈ 16,600 ppm dominant, methane/ethane high, acetylene ~7 ppm) points to a sustained high‑temperature thermal fault rather than arcing, which matches the suspected OLTC contact coking already on WO 1000051.

**Is the schedule dense enough for Condition 4?** No. IEEE C57.104 guidance for Condition 4 calls for daily sampling (or continuous online monitoring) when the rate is high, and at minimum weekly sampling even when the rate is low, together with an immediate engineering review and consideration of removing the unit from service. The current "schedule" is a single, unscheduled, unassigned confirmatory sample bundled into an OLTC inspection — so rather than freeing crew time, this transformer needs sampling *added*: schedule and assign WO 1000051 promptly and put a weekly (preferably daily until stabilized) DGA sampling routine in place. Note also that sample dates are 2024 while today is 2026‑09‑30, so the data are very stale; a fresh sample is the first priority.

## Disposition of each sampling job

| WO | Description | Priority | Acetylene/arcing mention | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection + confirmatory DGA oil sample, Transformer 1 | 1 | Yes (acetylene cited in long description) | **Kept** | Stability criteria failed (Condition 4), so no cancellations; also protected as priority 1 and mentions acetylene |

Even though the manual forecast was transparently labeled and the outcome would not change (Condition 4 fails regardless), the agent should have attempted the TSFM tools (or explicitly shown the attempt/failure) before falling back.
